instruction: Start only after task 0007-hostile-product-audit completes successfully. Implement the next Folio north-star milestone around high-volume intake, mobile capture, connectors, and AI automation. Research current Cloudflare R2/Workers limits and design uploads around direct-to-R2 presigned uploads so browser/mobile intake is not constrained by Worker request-body limits. Support computer file picker, drag-and-drop, mobile camera capture, mobile photo library, PDF/image/office-file intake where supported, background batch progress, retries, deduplication, checksums, tenant-safe object keys, and clear user-facing batch/file/storage limits. Add a visible upload-capacity message in the UI based on configured product limits rather than infrastructure maximums. Target a practical professional default such as hundreds of receipt/document files per batch with resumable/background processing, but derive and document the final limits from performance tests and AI-processing constraints. Add multi-receipt / multi-document camera capture: when one photo contains two or more receipts or clearly separate documents, use computer vision to detect boundaries, deskew, crop/segment them into distinct source records, preserve the original image for audit/evidence, and independently extract/validate each resulting document. The camera flow should support rapid continuous capture, 'scan another' without waiting on extraction, quality checks, flash/crop guidance, and background upload so the user takes the fewest possible photos. Add an inbox/import workspace for email attachments. Implement or strengthen provider-neutral connectors for Gmail/Google Calendar, Microsoft 365 mail/calendar/OneDrive/Excel, QuickBooks Online, and Wave where public APIs support the required operations, using OAuth, least privilege, encrypted tokens, revocation, sync cursors/webhooks where available, tenant isolation, and audit trails. Build a Day at a Glance / Today experience that combines appointments, deadlines, client follow-ups, unresolved document requests, unread/actionable communications, exceptions, and prioritized next actions. Build an autonomous-worker layer underneath the operating system. Workers may monitor connected inbox/calendar/accounting/document streams, classify and route intake, match documents and communications to clients, prepare Excel workbooks/exports and accounting sync actions, summarize threads, draft follow-up emails in the firm's configured voice, detect missing evidence, propose reminders and next actions, and execute low-risk administrative steps under explicit policy. Require approval or configured authorization before sending external communications, changing accounting/tax records, submitting filings, moving money, or making substantive tax/accounting decisions. Every autonomous action must be attributable, auditable, reversible where practical, idempotent, tenant-safe, and visible in a clear activity feed with reason/status. Optimize for software doing the preparation before Phyllis arrives, while preserving professional judgment. Do not invent unsupported integrations or silently scrape private portals. Add tests for multi-document segmentation, batch limits, camera/background intake, worker policy/approval boundaries, connector authorization, tenant isolation, retries/idempotency, and audit trails. Run typecheck, full test suite, production build, Wrangler dry-run, and update product docs with exact upload limits, multi-receipt capture behavior, worker capabilities, approval boundaries, and connector capabilities. Commit and push to main. Do not deploy production.
